top.title: Ex-captain Moody joins England in emotional haka response
top.description: Lewis Moody walked with current England captain Maro Itoje to join England's side to face New Zealand's haka [Getty Images] Former England captain Lewis Moody joined the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium. Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) last year, stood at the centre of England's line-up - between captain Maro Itoje and one of the team's vice-captains, Ellis Genge - as they faced up to the traditional pre-match challenge. Led by Genge's fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George, England then advanced to form a V shape, similar to the formation they took before last year's victory and the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final win against the All Blacks. Moody, who was embraced by most of England's team in the aftermath of the challenge and its acceptance, also delivered the match ball. Superb England run up record win over New Zealand England stars to help launch Moody MND challenge at All Blacks match With Twickenham energised, England started the match fast, with Henry Slade getting on the end of a Fin Smith grubber kick to score the first try after just four minutes. They went on to win 37-12, which was a record margin of victory for England over New Zealand. England coach Steve Borthwick told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It was particularly significant. What was really powerful was Lewis did the shirt presentations last night and he spoke unbelievably in the way he put his message across and it really resonated with the players. "It was some way to start a big game of rugby." All of England's players wore boots emblazoned with the logo of Moody's Front Up to MND campaign, to which signed warm-up and match-worn shirts will be donated. The campaign's first fundraising drive is a mass-participation coastal walk in June, which aims to raise more than £1m to fund research into the disease. A statement from England Rugby said: "As a hugely respected former England captain, it was important to the England men's team to show their support for Lewis and to involve him in many areas of the match day, including on the pitch. "Supporting Lewis and Front Up reflects the game's commitment to standing alongside those affected by MND, and to help raise awareness and funds for research." Moody delivered the match ball before England's victory over Australia last autumn, a few weeks after he revealed his diagnosis in an interview with BBC Breakfast. Last weekend, Wales players were bathed in red light and smoke during the All Blacks' haka in a response that was 'a year in the making'.

top.title: Matanović the difference maker as Freiburg extract victory in Elversberg
top.description: Matanović the difference maker as Freiburg extract victory in Elversberg Despite failing to muster up their best this afternoon, SC Freiburg secured a hard-fought 1-0 win over SV Elversberg. Igor Matanović pounced on one of very few chances for the visitors to leave the Saarland with three points. Scoring opportunities were few and far between in the Saarland as both teams fought for control. Francis Onyeka's mazy run caused some panic for Freiburg on 17 minutes that required an intervention from Philipp Lienhart. The first shot on target eventually fell the way of the hosts midway through the half. David Mokwa connected with a Lukas Petkov corner, however Mio Backhaus showed sharp reactions to divert it over his own crossbar. Freiburg's offensive output barely improved as the second-half rolled on. Julian Schuster's men only managed to register five shots before the hour mark, of which none managed to test Elversberg shot-stopper Nicolas Kristof. Wagner's side seemed more likely to score, threatening again on the hour. Felix Keidel picked off a Backhaus clearance and laid it off to Onyeka. The Leverkusen loanee's last involvement was blocked by Maxi Eggestein. Nonetheless, the Breisgau side snatched a precious 1-0 lead. Lienhart's long ball caught out Maximilian Rohr. Jan-Niklas Beste pounced, assisting Igor Matanović who picked out the lower-right corner with sheer precision. The hosts threw on Maurice Krattenmacher and Tom Zimmerscheid in desperation. When Yuito Suzuki steered home, the game result appeared final. However, an offside call bailed out Elversberg to give them fighting hope. Ultimately, said hope would be extinguished upon the final whistle as Freiburg held out. The win sees the Breisgau club pull level with second-place Bayern Munich, equal on points with only goal difference separating the two.

top.title: Nmecha helps Dortmund beat Gladbach to top Bundesliga
top.description: Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha celebrates after scoring on Saturday. (INA FASSBENDER) Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday. Bayern Munich's 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha's late strike. Dortmund are now outright first on 24 points, with Bayern and Freiburg, who won 1-0 at Elversberg, locked on 22 points. Bayern also lost Harry Kane to injury in Friday's draw, with the Ballon d'Or winner set to miss several months after undergoing surgery on his injured ankle earlier on Saturday. Dortmund, who travel to Arsenal on Tuesday, knew victory would send them top but the 2024 Champions League finalists had few chances against a stubborn Gladbach. Nmecha, who scored twice in Dortmund's 2-1 win over Elversberg before the international break, looked most likely when his header forced a save from Daniel Batz. With 17 minutes left, Marcel Sabitzer chipped a free-kick inches wide of the post. Dortmund continued to push and Nmecha was on hand to knock a rebound through Batz's fingers and help the visitors snare a crucial three points. Igor Matanovic's 68th-minute strike helped Freiburg break down promoted Elversberg and move level with Bayern. Last season's Europa League finalists Freiburg stay one point ahead of fourth-placed RB Leipzig, who romped to a 5-1 victory at Union Berlin. Antonio Nusa, Romulo, Brajan Gruda, Rocco Reitz and Ridle Baku scored for Leipzig, who host Lens in the Champions League on Tuesday. Gruda was particularly impressive with a goal and an assist, just days after impressing for Jurgen Klopp's Germany with a goal and two assists versus the Netherlands on the other side of the German capital. Elsewhere, Afonso Moreira broke his Bundesliga duck with a brace in Bayer Leverkusen's 4-0 home win over Paderborn. Moreira had failed to find the net since his summer move from Lyon but scored Leverkusen's first two goals and laid on one for Ezequiel Fernandez. Patrik Schick also got a goal to move level with Niclas Fuellkrug atop the league goalscoring charts with nine goals. Jonathan Burkardt scored the only goal as Eintracht Frankfurt beat Hoffenheim at home. Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu saved a first-half Andrej Kramaric penalty to keep his remarkable spot-kick record alive. Atubolu has saved seven out of the 11 penalties he has faced, which is the best save percentage in the Bundesliga's 64-year history. top.description: Elliot Anderson and Ayyoub Bouaddi both joined Manchester City in the summer [Getty Images] There may have been some eyebrows raised before kick-off when Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca decided to drop club record signing Enzo Fernandez to the bench against Fulham. Fernandez's lengthy excursions back home to Argentina for their two fixtures during the international break may have been a factor in Maresca's thinking when selecting his starting XI for this game. If it was, the Italian refrained from giving that as a reason. "I just think for this game it's better having Ayyoub Bouaddi in there," he told TNT Sports shortly before kick-off. Even so, the move was a significant one as his side were in desperate need of victory after suffering three straight Premier League defeats. That winless streak extended to four after being held to a 1-1 draw. Maresca had an opportunity to fix the issues in his set-up during the two-week break and admitted on Friday he was searching for "more balance" in the "defensive line, midfield and up front". The pairing of the steady Bouaddi and all-action Elliot Anderson in the centre of the park was the crucial call, and it may have given Maresca some idea as to how to approach the forthcoming run of games. "Ayyoub with Elliot were both really good," said Maresca. "Today we used Elliot a bit more attacking midfielder, he arrived inside the box and scored a fantastic goal, he had three or four moments around the box where he was really dangerous. "It is another solution for us. In this moment, we are trying to know each other more as players and also to find the right solution." On the other side of the field is Hoffenheim - also led by an Austrian coach, Christian Ilzer - who have had a tight schedule split between the Bundesliga and UEFA Europa League, but managed to pick up points in four out of their last five matches. In the Bundesliga itself, Die Kraichgauer have managed six points out of a potential twelve through their last four matches, defeating Borussia Mönchengladbach (2-1) and FC Schalke 04 (2-1). In terms of head-to-head record between the two sides, Frankfurt went into this match 3-1-1 through the last five encounters. In all five matches, four goals were scored between the two sides. top.description: Tijjani Noslin (L) celebrates scoring Lazio's second goal against Lecce (Alberto PIZZOLI) Lazio will continue their surprise stay at the top of Serie A for at least another week after thumping Lecce 3-0 on Saturday to move four points clear at the summit. Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio extended their lead over Inter Milan -- at struggling Atalanta on Sunday night -- thanks to goals in each half from Tijjani Noslin and a late Davide Frattesi strike. It was a straightforward win in Rome over a Lecce team now winless in five matches, with just one point collected in that run. Lazio looked to be in turmoil heading into this season, with a long-standing fan protest against owner Claudio Lotito leaving the Stadio Olimpico sparsely populated for home matches. But they have dropped just four points since the start of the season and are yet to be beaten after 12 matches. Como stay six points behind the leaders in fourth with a 2-0 home win over Cagliari. Cesc Fabregas' team welcome AEK Athens in the Champions League on Tuesday before hosting Juventus next weekend. AC Milan will move back into the top four ahead of Como with a home win over high-flying Frosinone on Sunday. top.title: Spartans’ Senior Night Turns Ugly as Ducks Romp
top.description: Michigan State’s Jeremiah Favorite, below, and Jay Coyne FB Caleb Wheatland, left, tackle Oregon’s Simeon Price during the fourth quarter on Friday, Nov. 20, 2026 in East Lansing. On Friday night, a 45-7 loss to the No. 13 CFP-ranked Oregon Ducks concluded the final home game for Michigan State seniors. The result was a harsh end to a season filled with ups and downs for the Spartans at Spartan Stadium. Fans watched their team honor the seniors, but the scoreboard told a different story of a team that ran out of steam and healthy players. The loss dropped Michigan State to 3-8, marking its eighth defeat of the season. The Spartans had already fallen short of the standard six-win bowl-eligibility threshold before Friday’s game. Michigan State entered the game without starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic, while backup Cam Fancher was a game-time decision because of his lingering injury. Fancher ultimately did not play, leaving true freshman Kayd Coffman to make his second start of the season. The injury bug had plagued the Spartans all season, leaving the roster thin on both sides of the ball. Coffman finished 10-for-19 for 106 yards and threw one interception against a tough Oregon defense. Redshirt freshman Leo Hannan replaced him when he was pulled in the fourth quarter. A Season of Injuries Derails the Defense The defense tried to keep the game close early on, but the lack of depth became too much to handle. Just before halftime, Oregon caught Michigan State off guard with a fake field goal. Kicker Gage Hurych took the ball 15 yards into the end zone, giving the Ducks a 17-0 lead. The Ducks then pounded the Spartans in the second half to secure the win. The injury list for Michigan State was long, including key players like linebacker Jordan Hall and safety Devin Vaught. Even the starting left guard and top tight ends were missing from the lineup. Without these bodies, the Spartans could not stop Oregon’s running game or contain its passing attack. One specific play highlighted the struggle when Coffman tripped over his own feet on a failed fourth-down run. Another critical error came when Chrishon McCray muffed a punt, giving Oregon excellent field position. The mistakes gave Oregon valuable field position and helped the Ducks build a lead that Michigan State never seriously threatened. The muffed punt led to a field goal, while the failed fourth-down conversion cost the Spartans an opportunity to get back into the game. Oregon Keeps Playoff Hopes Alive For Oregon, the win was essential to keep their College Football Playoff dreams alive. The Ducks had suffered three unexpected losses earlier in the year, making this game a must-win to stay in the mix. A loss would have likely ended their title hopes, but this victory keeps them in the conversation. top.title: Three Keys for Northwestern field hockey vs. Maryland in the National Championship
top.description: Northwestern survived its second consecutive shootout on Friday, this time against UConn, to advance to Sunday’s National Championship. This will be the third matchup of the season between Terrapins and Wildcats. Northwestern has won both of the last two games. With the National Championship threepeat on the line, here are the keys for the Wildcats to take down Maryland once and for all. Stay aggressive At press conference after press conference, head coach Tracey Fuchs has emphasized the high press that has earned Northwestern so many goals throughout the season. In previous postseason wins, Northwestern has outhustled its opponents. It’s scored goals off steals and earned penalty corners by applying pressure in the circle even when they don’t have the ball. In the last game of the season, the ‘Cats need to leave it all on the field, and if they can do that on the high press, they can apply pressure that Maryland has not yet been able to respond to. Lean on the experience Northwestern’s seniors have already played in three National Championship games, so they know what it is like to be in this situation. On the other side of the ball, Maryland does not have a single player from the 2022 team that made the Final Four. In the biggest games, experience can sometimes be more important than skill. Players like Ashley Sessa — who has scored two game-winning shootout goals in the last two games — have proven they can stay calm under pressure. The whole team needs to follow on Sunday, but they should be well prepared by the veteran presence on the team. If it ain’t broke, don’t fix it Northwestern has won the last two national championships. They have defeated Maryland twice by a combined margin of five goals. They are 5-1 against the top 10 teams in the nation and have given up just two goals in the entire postseason. This team has shown this season that it deserves its No.1 ranking in the country. Sometimes its wins haven’t been pretty, and sometimes they’ve taken six rounds of shootout, but Northwestern has always found a way to get the job done. With that superiority comes expectations, but it also brings the knowledge that Fuchs does not need to change much for this team to be champion caliber. If Northwestern can simply play the way it has played all season, the threepeat is all but assured.

nigeria.title: 2027: You must stay the course for progress, Tinubu tells Oyo electorate
nigeria.description: By Adeola Badru President Bola Tinubu has urged the people of Oyo State to sustain their support for the All Progressives Congress, APC, ahead of the 2027 general elections, declaring that continuity was essential for Nigeria’s progress, prosperity and development. Tinubu, who spoke at the APC presidential campaign rally held at the historic Mapo Hall in Ibadan on Saturday, called on the electorate to remain steadfast in their support for the party, while promising increased investment in education, agriculture, industrialisation and electricity supply. The President also endorsed Senator Sharafadeen Alli as the APC’s governorship candidate in Oyo State, urging the electorate to vote for him in the forthcoming election. He said the people of Oyo State had overwhelmingly supported the APC in the previous election and should not abandon the party, stressing that their continued backing would help secure a better future for their children and generations yet unborn. The rally was preceded by the arrival of the President at the Ladoke Akintola Airport, Ibadan, where the Olubadan of Ibadanland, Oba Rashidi Ladoja, and other members of the Oyo State Council of Obas and Chiefs received him. Addressing the political gathering at Mapo Hall, Tinubu called on the electorate to sustain their loyalty to the APC, describing the party as their own political platform. “I just want to say thank you. Thank you for all you have been doing and all the support you have given to APC. APC is our party. It’s your party. Is it clear?” he said. The President reminded the electorate that they had overwhelmingly supported the APC in the previous election, urging them to remain committed to the party as the country prepares for another general election. “You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time. You must stay the course. You must. For the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development, for your children and our great-grandchildren,” the president said. He stressed that the decisions being taken by the present generation must create opportunities for future generations to benefit from the country’s development. “Our future children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria,” the President said. He added that the country must prioritise education and agriculture to ensure that younger generations had the opportunity to thrive. “We must give them the right education, invest in agriculture,” he said. nigeria.title: ‘I Guarantee You Improvement In Electricity,’ Tinubu Tells Nigerians At Oyo Presidential Campaign Rally
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has assured Nigerians of improved electricity supply, promising to address the country’s persistent power challenges. The President gave the assurance on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress (APC) campaign rally at Mapo Hall in Ibadan, Oyo State, ahead of the 2027 general elections. “We will continue to bring industry, you will see, and I guarantee you an improvement in electricity. Joseph Tegbe (Minister of Power) is working really hard with his team. You voted overwhelmingly for APC last time; you must stay the course for the sake of progress, prosperity of our country, development for the children and our great-grandchildren. Our future children must benefit from the hope of Nigeria. We must give them the right education and invest in Agriculture,” he said. ﻿ The President also announced plans to revive the defunct Leyland automobile factory in Ibadan through an agreement with Chinese bus manufacturer Yutong. “For Oyo State, we have signed an agreement with Yutong of China to reopen the old Leyland factory in Ibadan. We are reopening it to produce public transport and automobile assembly plant there,” he said. The agreement, signed on November 19, 2026, involves the Federal Government, through the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), Yutong and its local partner, YP Automobile. Electricity Challenges A depiction of a lantern and grid Tinubu’s latest assurance comes amid growing frustration among Nigerians over inadequate electricity supply, with households and businesses grappling with prolonged outages in different parts of the country. The shortages have renewed questions about the effectiveness of the Band A, B and C electricity tariff classification, which links customers’ payments to the minimum hours of electricity supply they are expected to receive. Customers on Band A, who are entitled to a minimum of 20 hours of electricity daily, have also complained about inadequate supply. Intense heat has compounded the situation, leaving many residents struggling to cope without electricity to run fans and air conditioners. Several Nigerians, including figures like Kate Henshaw and Cute Abiola, have expressed frustration over persistent power outages, lamenting that households have become “mini-factories” forced to generate their own electricity. Meanwhile, rising petrol and diesel prices have made generator use increasingly expensive, while the cost of installing solar panels, batteries and inverters remains beyond the reach of many households and small businesses. Minister of Power Tegbe recently attributed the prolonged blackouts to planned maintenance at the Egbin Power Station, gas supply shortages and vandalism of transmission infrastructure. nigeria.title: ‘Our Culture’: Deaf Nigerians Embrace Indigenous Sign Languages
nigeria.description: With a quick flick of the wrist, Umaru Zayyanu conveys the phrase “I am a Nigerian”. But the 37-year-old is not speaking — or signing, rather — in the official sign language, Nigerian Sign Language (NSL). Instead, he’s using Hausa sign language. Such indigenous sign languages abound in the country, where deaf people were communicating with each other long before the advent of formal sign language taught in deaf schools, in 1960. Today, Nigeria, like many countries on the continent with limited education budgets, has a hard enough time placing children in dedicated schools for the deaf and hard of hearing. And there’s even less attention paid to local sign languages used outside the school system — a serious disservice to the country’s linguistic diversity, Festus Zenda, who has worked on documentation projects with local deaf communities, told AFP. “These indigenous signing systems should be studied, documented and preserved before changes in education, migration, technology and wider use of Nigerian Sign Language cause some of them to decline or disappear,” said Zenda, who has helped document the local sign language used by the Tiv ethnic group, in Benue state. A deaf resident gestures with his fingers while conversing during a community meeting in Zuba, near Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Sani Lawali (3R), a deaf resident gestures with his hands while conversing during a community meeting in Zuba, near Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Festus Zenda, Deaf Advocate and Indigenous Sign Language Promoter, with Nigeria’s National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP), uses sign language to converse during a video call along a street in Abuja, on October 16, 2026. (Photo by LIGHT ORIYE TAMUNOTONYE / AFP) Displacement by formal signing The working-class Abuja exurb of Zuba is a symphony of motorcycle horns, plantain hawkers’ shouts and the dull hum of construction work. Another group adds their own, milder contributions: claps, muffled shouts of exclamation and the swish of rapid hand gestures as they chat in Hausa signs. Nigerian sign languages, like their spoken counterparts, are sometimes confined to a small number of speakers in a country crowded with some 500 tongues and an unknown number of sign languages. But Hausa sign language has become a lingua franca for deaf people across the north of the country. “I cherish my culture, I cherish my indigenous sign language,” Sanni Lawal, who runs a laundry business in Zuba’s crowded market, told AFP through an interpreter. “I want it to expand everywhere.” Nigeria traces its official sign language to Andrew Foster, an American who introduced formal deaf education across a swathe of African countries at the dawn of independence from colonial powers. nigeria.title: 2027: Reset your mind, align with people’s choice, Oshiomhole tells Makinde
nigeria.description: By Adeola Badru Senator Adams Oshiomhole, former Governor of Edo State, has urged Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, to reconsider his political position ahead of the 2027 general elections, saying the country needed leaders committed to sustaining progress. Oshiomhole, who spoke in Ibadan on Saturday during President Bola Tinubu’s rally at the historic Mapo Hall, challenged Makinde to align himself with the wishes of the electorate, insisting that the governor must first reconsider his own position on Tinubu’s re-election bid. The former Edo governor, who expressed support for Tinubu’s second-term ambition, described the forthcoming election as a decisive moment for Nigeria and questioned whether Makinde’s call for a reset was intended to reverse policies he said had benefited ordinary Nigerians. “This coming election is a decisive factor. We have a leader, the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. Oshiomhole said he had questions for Makinde over his position on Tinubu’s continuation in office, particularly regarding the administration’s student loan scheme, infrastructure development, and improved welfare for university lecturers. He asked whether Makinde’s opposition to the president’s re-election was connected to the federal government’s decision to provide financial assistance to students from poor backgrounds through the student loan scheme. “Is Seyi Makinde angry because Tinubu is giving loans to the children of poor people in our universities? Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he asked. The senator also questioned whether the governor intended to reverse the federal government’s infrastructure projects, particularly the coastal highway linking Lagos to Calabar, which he said would improve connectivity and make movement easier for Nigerians. “The President is creating massive infrastructure to connect Lagos to Calabar so that our people can move. Is that what Makinde wants to reset?” he said. Oshiomhole further challenged Makinde’s position on the welfare of university lecturers, citing the University of Ibadan as an example of an institution that had previously experienced repeated disruptions to its academic calendar due to industrial action. He recalled that university lecturers had, in the past, frequently embarked on strikes, disrupting academic activities and delaying students’ graduation. “For this city has the most outstanding university in Africa, the University of Ibadan. For a long, long time, the lecturer will teach you for two days and then will go on strike for three days. Is that not true?” he said. nigeria.title: Outrage as Defence Ministry publicises APC campaign rally
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Ministry of Defence has come under criticism on social media after its official X account published details of preparations for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally in support of President Bola Tinubu’s 2027 re-election bid. In a post on Saturday, it announced that the rally was scheduled to hold at Mapo Hall, Ibadan, Oyo State, on November 21, 2026, with Tinubu and key party officials expected to attend. It also disclosed that the Minister of Defence, retired General Christopher Musa, had visited the venue on Friday night to assess security arrangements and other preparations ahead of the event. “Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), OFR, Friday night conducted an on-the-spot inspection of the venue as part of strategic preparations ahead of the upcoming presidential campaign rally in the state,” the post reads. “During the visit, General Musa toured the premises and surrounding perimeters to evaluate security readiness, crowd management logistics, and overall infrastructural preparedness. President Bola Tinubu GCFR, and key party officials would be on ground for the rally.” Defence Ministry/X Defence Ministry/X The post, which was accompanied by photographs of the minister’s inspection, was followed by criticism from several Nigerians, who questioned the use of an official government platform to publicise the activities of a political party. One of the critics, Kunle Adebajo, described the development as “political psychosis so deep it’s ridiculous even by Nigerian standards”. Another X user, N6, questioned the ministry’s apparent involvement in partisan activities, asking, “How is the Ministry of Defence handle clearly being Partisan. nigeria.title: Haaland in VAR controversy as Man City held by Fulham
nigeria.description: Erling Haaland was controversially denied a crucial goal as Manchester City’s spluttering Premier League title challenge suffered a fresh blow in a 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday. Enzo Maresca’s side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz’s early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland’s equaliser was contentiously ruled out. The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line. But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision. Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season. But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time. Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday. After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches. It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham. Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks. Maresca has claimed City are not bothered by the “noise” around the financial scandal, which is likely to include a huge points deduction if the appeal fails. But his team’s lethargic performances of late suggest otherwise, with tricky tests against Napoli on Tuesday and Arsenal next weekend threatening to extend their slump. – Slumping City – City needed a fast start to ease their anxiety and Erling Haaland almost delivered it when his looping header was cleared off the line. But Maresca has failed to fix the defensive problems that ailed City in their previous three games. Fulham took full advantage of City’s flaws to snatch the lead with an incisive counter in the 16th minute. Former City winger Oscar Bobb pounced on a wayward pass and accelerated down the right flank before picking out Muniz’s run into the penalty area. With City’s defence in disarray, Muniz kept his composure to curl a fine finish into the top corner. Maresca turned away in disgust and his frustration only increased when City were denied a leveller in the 26th minute. Iliman Ndiaye’s cross reached Haaland inside the six-yard box but the Norway striker’s weak volley was saved by Leno. Haaland’s momentum carried him into Leno and he kicked the ball over the line as the Fulham keeper struggled to get hold of it. But Haaland’s celebrations were curtailed by VAR’s decision to disallow the goal for a foul on Leno. Haaland squandered a golden opportunity to drag City level when he blazed wildly over from Phil Foden’s defence splitting pass. nigeria.title: Diallo present as African football boss Motsepe reiterates support for Infantino
nigeria.description: African football supremo Patrice Motsepe said Saturday that all 54 members of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) support Gianni Infantino’s bid for re-election as FIFA president. Motsepe made the declaration in Abuja, where CAF is holding its ordinary general assembly and at which one of Infantino’s two rivals, French football chief Philippe Diallo is present. Former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima is the other candidate. The trio will learn whether they have been successful on March 18 next year in Rabat — the winning candidate must obtain a majority of the 211 associations. CAF’s support for Infantino comes hours after another of his steadfast supporters South American football’s governing body CONMEBOL gave him their “unanimous” backing. CAF has been consistently behind Infantino — who is seeking a fourth and final term — even after the furore he stirred up in July with his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 World Cup. “Gianni, you have our support on behalf of the 54 nations in Africa to be our candidate,” Motsepe said. “I have a report from all 54 member associations in Africa to say that we are unanimously supporting Gianni.” Infantino has faced multiple calls to step down and lost the backing of European football’s governing body UEFA, whilst CONCACAF has also been strident in its criticism of the 56-year-old Swiss lawyer. Motsepe though has been a vocal supporter and Infantino said such loyalty was reciprocal. “You will always find, in me and in FIFA, a trusted partner,” Infantino told the assembly, announcing cash inflow of $25 million to each member of CAF, starting January 2027 for development projects. On Wednesday, UEFA vice-president Laura McAllister told AFP that Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at the 1960 Olympics in Rome, should not be seen as solely a European candidate. “He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF countries,” she said. McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of UEFA, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc. “There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda,” the 61-year-old said. “There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands. “This applies everywhere in world football. nigeria.description: Mexico’s military announced on Saturday that it had captured the leader of a drug-trafficking group who was among the 10 most-wanted fugitives sought by US law enforcement. A firefight ensued between the military and gang members in the town of Guasave, sparking panic in the surrounding area, including at a professional baseball game, local media reported. “Chapo Isidro” is the alleged leader of the Beltran Leyva gang, which is allied with one of two rival factions in the powerful Sinaloa cartel, Mexico’s military said. He was captured alongside his number two in the group and another man identified as a financial operator. They were all transported by a Mexican Air Force aircraft to Mexico City “to be placed at the disposal of the competent prosecutorial authorities,” the military said. Chapo Isidro faces criminal charges in both Mexico and the United States. The FBI had placed him on its list of 10 most wanted fugitives and offered a $5 million reward for information leading to his arrest. nigeria.description: The Federal Government has increased annual admission into medical schools from 5,000 to 12,000 students, the Minister of Education, Dr. Tunji Alausa, has said. Alausa, who stated this on the sidelines of the inauguration of a 192-bed hostel at the College of Medicine, University of Ibadan (UI), on Saturday, said that it targets enrollment of 20,000 students annually. The minister said the increase in enrollment was part of efforts to address manpower shortages in the health sector amid the migration of Nigerian medical professionals abroad. He said that the government, since President Bola Tinubu assumed office, had increased nursing enrollment from about 28,000 annually to more than 130,000. According to him, the country is making progress in producing more healthcare professionals. Alausa, who represented Tinubu at the inauguration, said the administration was investing in infrastructure to expand the capacity of medical schools and other tertiary institutions to accommodate more students. According to him, annual admission into medical schools has risen to about 12,000, from 5,000 students recorded before the administration began in May 2023. “We decided that in four years, we will increase the number to 20,000 annually. “Three years into it, we are enrolling about 12,000 medical students now across all our medical schools in the country, and by the end of 2028, we will meet our target of enrolling over 20,000 medical students,” he said. Alausa said the government had also increased admission into dentistry, pharmacy, physiotherapy, and other allied health programs to strengthen the country’s healthcare workforce. He said the expansion was being complemented by investments in infrastructure, including hostels, to support increased enrollment and improve the learning environment. The minister added that the government was also investing in the education sector through the Nigeria Education Sector Renewal Initiative. “This includes the construction and rehabilitation of schools, expansion of medical schools, and re-equipping of engineering workshops,” the minister said. Alausa said the administration had invested nearly N500 billion in educational infrastructure, adding that the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) had also expanded access to tertiary education for students irrespective of their economic backgrounds. He urged journalists to verify the figures on nursing and medical student enrollment through the relevant regulatory bodies, including the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. nigeria.title: The Governor, The Candidate And The Voter
nigeria.description: Anambra puts the power of endorsements to the test, while opposition negotiations and election safeguards face approaching deadlines. On Thursday in Awka, Governor Chukwuma Soludo presented APGA’s flag to Vice-President Kashim Shettima, who received it on behalf of President Bola Tinubu. On Friday, Peter Obi took his campaign through Onitsha, attracting supporters ahead of his town hall engagement. Two neighbouring cities offered competing pictures of political strength. In Awka, the message was partnership with the centre. In Onitsha, Obi demonstrated his continuing ability to mobilise in the state he once governed. The electoral question lies between those pictures: how far can a governor’s endorsement move presidential votes, and how effectively can a candidate convert personal loyalty into turnout? Anambra will help answer both. Soludo’s Wager APGA’s support gives Tinubu an organised partner outside the APC. Soludo is making an argument about the South-East’s place in national politics: that cooperation with the President offers a route to influence and development. The presentation reaffirmed APGA’s presidential alignment while the party continues pursuing its own interests in other elections. For Tinubu, the opportunity lies in improving his reach through a political organisation rooted in the state. For Soludo, the challenge is to persuade people who support his governorship to make the same choice in a presidential contest. Those loyalties need not coincide. Voters can approve of a governor’s performance and prefer another presidential candidate. They can also reconsider a previous choice if a new alliance offers a convincing case. The evidence will emerge through sustained mobilisation, local organisation and ultimately the ballot. A flag presentation establishes an endorsement. It cannot establish the electorate’s response. Obi’s Home-State Test Obi’s Onitsha road show supplies evidence of campaign activity and visible support. It does not, on its own, measure the balance of opinion across Anambra. His task is to maintain that support while building sufficient reach elsewhere. The home-state contest also brings his governing record into sharper focus. Obi has chosen to defend that record publicly; Soludo is advancing a different argument about Anambra’s political interests. Voters deserve an exchange grounded in verifiable achievements, present needs and credible proposals. Claims that cooperation necessarily delivers prosperity or that popular enthusiasm guarantees victory require testing. Anambra’s significance extends beyond its presidential tally. It offers a clear case study in the relationship between party machinery, a governor’s influence and a candidate’s personal following. nigeria.title: Nigeria endorses Infantino for another term as FIFA president
nigeria.description: Nigeria has declared its support for Gianni Infantino’s bid to retain the presidency of the world football governing body, FIFA, in the 2027 election. The Chairman of the National Sports Commission, Shehu Dikko, announced the Federal Government’s endorsement on Saturday during the 48th Ordinary General Assembly of the Confederation of African Football in Abuja. Speaking on behalf of President Bola Tinubu, Dikko said Nigeria would back Infantino’s re-election and called on other African football associations to support his continued leadership. “I must make it clear here on behalf of the Federal Government and in regard to the resolution of all the members of CAF that Nigeria firmly endorses Mr Gianni Infantino’s candidacy for the election. “This is a direct message that was given to us by the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Federal Republic of Nigeria,” he said. “We recognise Mr Gianni’s contribution to the advancement of football worldwide, particularly in Africa, and urge our fellow African member associations to stand firmly together in support of his continued leadership. “This is in our collective interest,” he added. The NSC chairman also praised Infantino’s administration, drawing on his experience in football management to argue that the FIFA president’s decisions had served the interests of the sport. “Before I conclude, if I put my heart as a football person, Mr President, as a former member of the NFL Exco, Chairman of the League, member of the FIFA Seconders Committee, and founding member of the World League Forum, I must tell you, Gianni’s decisions are very, very good for football. They are very apt for football,” he said. He maintained that Infantino’s central responsibility was to grow the game and generate more revenue, arguing that disagreements within football administration largely concerned how the funds were shared. “His main job is to develop football and bring revenues to football. He tries to do that. The entire issue we are seeing across the world here today has nothing to do with bringing the revenues or the distribution. It’s all about distributing these revenues,” Dikko said. Nigeria’s declaration came at the same gathering where CAF president Patrice Motsepe reiterated the continental body’s backing for Infantino’s re-election. Infantino, who became FIFA president in 2016, is seeking another four-year term at the election scheduled to hold in Morocco in March 2027 with French Football Federation president Philippe Diallo and Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima set to challenge him. business.title: SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine SEC Freezes Assets in $560 Million Crypto Trading Ponzi Scheme The Securities and Exchange Commission has frozen the assets of Indianapolis-based Backward Hat Capital and its two co-founders, saying the firm ran a $560 million Ponzi scheme that told investors their money would be turned into crypto and used for AI-driven currency trading. The agency said Backward Hat, co-founders Phillip Williams and Devin Johnson, Johnson’s firm Traders Point Capital and Joseph Anderson raised the money from more than 2,000 investors starting in July 2022. A federal court granted a temporary restraining order, an asset freeze and expedited discovery to halt what the SEC called an ongoing scheme. Federal prosecutors in New York and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission brought parallel cases. The SEC and CFTC suits were filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana, and the CFTC said the court has appointed Kevin B. Duff as temporary receiver to take control of the companies and the individual defendants’ assets. The pitch: crypto, AI and 6% a month According to the SEC’s complaint , Williams and Johnson sold limited partnership interests in private funds through a network of promoters, including to Williams’s former investment advisory clients. They promised a proprietary, “AI-driven” algorithm that supposedly returned at least 6% every month by trading foreign exchange. Investor money, the pitch went, would first be converted into a crypto asset and then used for that arbitrage. The complaint does not name bitcoin as the asset. It says about $109 million of the roughly $210 million raised from July 2022 to September 2025 was sent to the fund’s Coinbase account and converted. Of that, more than $56 million went to personal crypto accounts held by Williams, Johnson and a relief defendant, according to the complaint. About $40 million ended up on three platforms where some of it was used to trade other crypto assets, but little to no money was used to trade FX. After October 2025, the scheme raised about $350 million, and none of it was sent to Coinbase. Where the money went The SEC said the defendants made more than $250 million in Ponzi payments to earlier investors and moved more than $220 million to themselves. The money paid for exotic cars, expensive homes, private air travel and other businesses they owned, and helped feed Johnson’s gambling. Promoters took more than $50 million. Anderson is accused of producing fake financial reports, including at least two “audit reports” and a “quality of earnings” report from a supposedly independent firm. The SEC said the documents falsely claimed the returns had been verified against bank and brokerage records. It said Anderson did no audit work, was not independent and had a financial stake in the scheme. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Featuring more than 25 productions, international performances from Kenya, Brazil, Norway and Canada, high-profile diplomatic engagements and a spectacular Opening Night Gala, the festival reinforced its growing position as an important platform for showcasing Nigerian creativity and connecting global theatre communities. The impressive turnout, diversity of productions and international participation demonstrated the growing appetite for live theatre and the potential of cultural platforms to stimulate creative enterprise, encourage international collaboration and strengthen Nigeria’s global cultural presence. A Vision For Global Recognition Speaking on the success of the festival, Founder and Creative Producer, Bolanle Austen-Peters , said: “Our ambition has always been to create more than a theatre festival. We want to build a platform that places Lagos firmly on the global cultural map, gives African stories the international visibility they deserve and creates meaningful opportunities for our artists. Welcoming over 20,000 attendees, presenting more than 25 productions and bringing international performers from four countries to Lagos is a powerful affirmation of this vision. Theatre is not just entertainment; it is an instrument of cultural identity, economic opportunity and global influence. The Stage Is Everywhere, and Africa must claim its rightful place on that stage.” A Week Of Culture And Collaboration The festival opened on November 9 with Theatre Meets Food at Kaly Restaurant, featuring celebrated chef Hilda Baci in a unique fusion of culinary artistry and live performance. The week also featured diplomatic and cultural engagements hosted by the United States Consul General in Lagos and the British Embassy, alongside a networking reception organised by the British Council for festival directors and participating production companies. These engagements highlighted the importance of international partnerships and cultural diplomacy in advancing Nigeria’s creative industry. A Celebration Of Excellence A major highlight was the Opening Night Gala, held on November 13 at Shell Hall, MUSON Centre, which welcomed over 1,000 guests, including the Governor of Lagos State, Babajide Olusola Sanwo-Olu ; the Chargé d’Affaires of the US Mission in Nigeria; the US Consul General; the British Deputy High Commissioner; the Consul General of Brazil; the Consul General of South Africa, the Ambassador of the Republic of Korea; alongside other members of the diplomatic corps, heads of institutions, government representatives, international delegates and leading figures in the creative industry. entertainment.title: A Safari, a Beach & Easy Entry? 5 African Spots for Your Christmas Holiday
entertainment.description: Five African destinations Nigerian passport holders can visit visa-free or with visa on arrival this Christmas holiday. Image: AI-generated. The group chat has the concerts, the dinners and the Detty December link-ups covered. But has anyone planned the getaway? Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Whether you are travelling solo, gathering your friends, taking the family along or joining a curated travel group, here are five destinations worth considering for your Christmas holiday. Kenya Imagine spotting lions and giraffes against a city skyline before breakfast, then catching an evening flight or train straight to the coast for fresh seafood by the Indian Ocean. That contrast is what makes Kenya such a rewarding December escape. Nairobi gives you immediate access to wildlife at Nairobi National Park and the Giraffe Centre alongside lively restaurants and art spaces in Westlands and Karen, while longer itineraries open up classic game drives in the Maasai Mara, views of Mount Kilimanjaro in Amboseli, and warm beach days in Diani or Watamu. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. Rwanda Not everyone wants their year-end holiday to feel like a non-stop sprint, and Rwanda is built for travellers who prefer scenery, clean air, and an unhurried pace. Days in Kigali easily revolve around specialty coffee shops, contemporary art at Inema Arts Center, and a sobering, essential visit to the Kigali Genocide Memorial before you head out into the countryside. From the capital, you can track chimpanzees and walk above the trees in Nyungwe Forest, go on wildlife drives in Akagera National Park, or spend quiet afternoons along the shores of Lake Kivu. With 30-day visa-free entry for Nigerian passport holders, getting there is straightforward from start to finish. Mauritius Sometimes a proper Christmas break calls for leaving mainland schedules behind altogether for turquoise lagoons, catamaran cruises, and mountain trails. In Mauritius, you can base yourself around Grand Baie in the north for boat trips to Île aux Cerfs and lively beachside dinners, or head south-west toward Le Morne Brabant for coastal hikes and water sports. Between beach days, the bustling Central Market in Port Louis, the lush trails of Black River Gorges National Park, and Casela Nature Parks keep a week-long itinerary full without ever feeling hectic. entertainment.title: Esther Adeyanju: This International Men’s Day, Let’s Make Room for Men’s Vulnerability
entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. entertainment.title: How La Roche-Posay Brought Skin Science to Over 500 Guests in Its First Living Lab Experience
entertainment.description: La Roche-Posay concluded its first Living Lab experience in Nigeria, welcoming Nigerian stakeholders to its opening party and three-day programme, held from 4 to 6 November 2026 at Oasis by The Five Palm, Victoria Island, Lagos. Inspired by the original Living Lab concept in Paris, the experience brought the science, research and expertise behind skincare closer to Nigerian consumers and healthcare professionals. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Each day featured three expert-led sessions exploring the role of dermatology and scientific research in advancing skin health, the wider impact of skin conditions on everyday life, and the importance of understanding product safety, tolerance and efficacy. The sessions brought together healthcare professionals and representatives from across Nigeria’s dermatological beauty and skincare community, encouraging knowledge-sharing and stronger connections between science, expertise and consumer education. Visitors explored five dedicated Innovation Corners showcasing La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Mela B3, Anthelios, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges. Each space introduced visitors to specific skin concerns and the science behind the brand’s product formulations. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Beyond the Innovation Corners, visitors explored the Blue House, which presented La Roche-Posay’s history and commitment to dermatological innovation, and the Scars of Life Cinema. The cinema screened a 25-minute film exploring the physical and psychological realities of living with scars and scarring, including their impact on self-image and everyday life. The film also highlighted how Lipikar supports the care of skin affected by scarring, bringing attention to the importance of addressing both the visible and less visible experiences associated with skin conditions. The programme also created opportunities for visitors to engage with skincare experts and dermatologists through one-on-one consultations, ask questions about their individual skin concerns and receive guidance on building appropriate skincare routines. entertainment.description: One of the best aspects of art is its ability to imitate current events or imagine possibilities. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. At its core, art exists to entertain, inform and critique society. Through films, music and visual expressions, we are continually reminded of our shared humanity—our joys, flaws and contradictions. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Nonetheless, some films have attempted to explore what it means to be a man in today’s world. They invite audiences to contemplate important questions such as: What is the role of men in society? What defines a man? How does a man’s behaviour influence those around him? What expectations does society place on men? What responsibilities do men have within society? Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. It challenges traditional expectations of masculinity by illustrating a father’s journey through uncertainty, learning empathy, and committing to being present for his child/ren. entertainment.description: What does it really mean to play to win in business and leadership? Beyond earning a seat at the table, it requires more than competence or professional accomplishments. It requires the confidence to own one’s value, the clarity to communicate one’s contributions and the intentionality to build visibility that translates into meaningful influence. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. Convened by Bola Matel-Okoh , a dual-qualified attorney (called to both the New York and Nigerian Bars), Executive Coach, Non-Executive Director at Wema Bank, and CEO of BMO Advisory Services , the second edition of the summit was themed Playing to Win: Elevate Your Vision, Value and Visibility. It provided an intentional platform for candid conversations, practical insights and strategic alliances on what it takes for women to advance, lead and thrive in today’s evolving corporate landscape. In her opening address, Matel-Okoh challenged women to rethink how they approach professional visibility, authority and advancement. According to her, competence is merely the baseline; it is not enough if you are unwilling to communicate your value, own your voice and position yourself for higher-stakes opportunities. This philosophy also came through in her cover interview with THISDAY Glitterati ahead of the summit, where she offered a compelling perspective on the distinction between holding a powerful position and exercising genuine influence. “A powerful position gives you formal authority. Influence determines how deeply your leadership shapes people’s thinking, decisions and actions. A title may secure your place in a meeting, but credibility makes people listen,” she explained. She also challenged the assumption that excellent work will automatically speak for itself, encouraging women to communicate their contributions with evidence and confidence. “What problem did you solve? What result did you produce? What changed because of your leadership?” she asked, highlighting the importance of making professional value visible to the decision-makers who influence career progression and boardroom opportunities. “There is no need to diminish your achievements to make others comfortable. You can be gracious and still be clear about the value you bring,” she added. entertainment.title: Tochukwu Ekoh: What My Friend’s Passing Taught Me About Kindness
entertainment.description: A thoughtful young woman sits in a relaxed pose in a serene bedroom, reflecting peacefully. Photo credit: Alex Green/Pexels. I lost someone recently, and since then, I have found myself revisiting little moments, conversations and encounters I probably would not have given much thought to otherwise. We weren’t particularly close , or I wouldn’t describe our relationship that way . We had reconnected after a long time and started seeing each other more often, especially after I resumed work following an accident I was involved in. He gradually became part of my daily routine. Whenever I went to work, he would come to pick me up from the office, and we would go home together. In many ways, he looked out for me and made sure I got home safely. We started talking more. We would discuss life, share experiences and occasionally open up about things happening in our individual lives. There was also an emotional dimension to our friendship. He was interested in me romantically, I realised, but I didn’t feel the same way. I tried to understand my feelings, but the truth was that I simply wasn’t in love with him. I couldn’t manufacture feelings that weren’t there. Then I heard that he passed away. My first reaction, strangely, was guilt. I began asking myself: Was I a good friend to him? Was I kind enough? Was I considerate? Did I treat him well? Could I have done something differently? I caught myself wondering whether I should have given him a chance . Perhaps I should have allowed him to love me. But then would I have done that out of genuine affection or simply out of pity? And would that have been fair to either of us? My understanding is that not returning someone’s romantic feelings does not mean we cannot offer them genuine friendship, kindness and compassion. I didn’t owe him romantic love, but I could have been a good friend. That has stayed with me. Beyond the guilt, there was another question I couldn’t get out of my head: Why did God allow us to reconnect? Why, after such a long time, did our paths have to cross again? Why did we have to start talking, sharing experiences and becoming familiar with each other again, only for him to die shortly afterwards? Why him? Why at that particular time? What was the reason for that reconnection, and why did it have to end this way? The timing of certain events leaves you with more questions than answers. What makes this loss even more difficult to comprehend is how it happened. I had been the one who suffered an accident, yet I survived and was gradually recovering. He wasn’t sick. entertainment.description: Entertainment Week Africa (EWA) , the pan-African platform for the business of creativity, opens its fifth edition in Lagos tomorrow, Wednesday, 18 November. The programme runs until Saturday, 21 November, and brings together creators, executives, investors, policymakers and delegations from more than 18 African countries. This year’s theme, Five Years of Closing the Gap, reflects the purpose EWA was built around: connecting African talent with the capital, markets, skills and audiences it needs to grow. Since its first edition, EWA has welcomed more than 67,800 attendees. entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. sports.title: Ex-captain Moody joins England in emotional haka response
sports.description: Lewis Moody walked with current England captain Maro Itoje to join England's side to face New Zealand's haka [Getty Images] Former England captain Lewis Moody joined the current team to face New Zealand's haka in an emotional start to Saturday's Test match at Allianz Stadium. Moody, who was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (MND) last year, stood at the centre of England's line-up - between captain Maro Itoje and one of the team's vice-captains, Ellis Genge - as they faced up to the traditional pre-match challenge. Led by Genge's fellow vice-captains Ollie Chessum and Jamie George, England then advanced to form a V shape, similar to the formation they took before last year's victory and the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final win against the All Blacks. Moody, who was embraced by most of England's team in the aftermath of the challenge and its acceptance, also delivered the match ball. Superb England run up record win over New Zealand England stars to help launch Moody MND challenge at All Blacks match With Twickenham energised, England started the match fast, with Henry Slade getting on the end of a Fin Smith grubber kick to score the first try after just four minutes. They went on to win 37-12, which was a record margin of victory for England over New Zealand. England coach Steve Borthwick told BBC Radio 5 Live: "It was particularly significant. What was really powerful was Lewis did the shirt presentations last night and he spoke unbelievably in the way he put his message across and it really resonated with the players. "It was some way to start a big game of rugby." All of England's players wore boots emblazoned with the logo of Moody's Front Up to MND campaign, to which signed warm-up and match-worn shirts will be donated. The campaign's first fundraising drive is a mass-participation coastal walk in June, which aims to raise more than £1m to fund research into the disease. A statement from England Rugby said: "As a hugely respected former England captain, it was important to the England men's team to show their support for Lewis and to involve him in many areas of the match day, including on the pitch. "Supporting Lewis and Front Up reflects the game's commitment to standing alongside those affected by MND, and to help raise awareness and funds for research." Moody delivered the match ball before England's victory over Australia last autumn, a few weeks after he revealed his diagnosis in an interview with BBC Breakfast. Last weekend, Wales players were bathed in red light and smoke during the All Blacks' haka in a response that was 'a year in the making'.

sports.title: Matanović the difference maker as Freiburg extract victory in Elversberg
sports.description: Matanović the difference maker as Freiburg extract victory in Elversberg Despite failing to muster up their best this afternoon, SC Freiburg secured a hard-fought 1-0 win over SV Elversberg. Igor Matanović pounced on one of very few chances for the visitors to leave the Saarland with three points. Scoring opportunities were few and far between in the Saarland as both teams fought for control. Francis Onyeka's mazy run caused some panic for Freiburg on 17 minutes that required an intervention from Philipp Lienhart. The first shot on target eventually fell the way of the hosts midway through the half. David Mokwa connected with a Lukas Petkov corner, however Mio Backhaus showed sharp reactions to divert it over his own crossbar. Freiburg's offensive output barely improved as the second-half rolled on. Julian Schuster's men only managed to register five shots before the hour mark, of which none managed to test Elversberg shot-stopper Nicolas Kristof. Wagner's side seemed more likely to score, threatening again on the hour. Felix Keidel picked off a Backhaus clearance and laid it off to Onyeka. The Leverkusen loanee's last involvement was blocked by Maxi Eggestein. Nonetheless, the Breisgau side snatched a precious 1-0 lead. Lienhart's long ball caught out Maximilian Rohr. Jan-Niklas Beste pounced, assisting Igor Matanović who picked out the lower-right corner with sheer precision. The hosts threw on Maurice Krattenmacher and Tom Zimmerscheid in desperation. When Yuito Suzuki steered home, the game result appeared final. However, an offside call bailed out Elversberg to give them fighting hope. Ultimately, said hope would be extinguished upon the final whistle as Freiburg held out. The win sees the Breisgau club pull level with second-place Bayern Munich, equal on points with only goal difference separating the two.

sports.description: Dortmund midfielder Felix Nmecha celebrates after scoring on Saturday. (INA FASSBENDER) Felix Nmecha scored with 10 minutes remaining to send Borussia Dortmund to the top of the Bundesliga table with a 1-0 win at Borussia Moenchengladbach on Saturday. Bayern Munich's 1-1 home draw with Cologne on Friday opened up the door for the chasers but Dortmund had few opportunities until Nmecha's late strike. With 17 minutes left, Marcel Sabitzer chipped a free-kick inches wide of the post. Dortmund continued to push and Nmecha was on hand to knock a rebound through Batz's fingers and help the visitors snare a crucial three points. Igor Matanovic's 68th-minute strike helped Freiburg break down promoted Elversberg and move level with Bayern. Last season's Europa League finalists Freiburg stay one point ahead of fourth-placed RB Leipzig, who romped to a 5-1 victory at Union Berlin. sports.title: Man City boss Maresca fumes over Haaland controversy in Fulham draw
sports.description: Manchester City striker Erling Haaland had a crucial goal disallowed against Fulham (Oli SCARFF) Enzo Maresca insisted it was "quite clear" that Erling Haaland was wrongly denied a crucial goal in Manchester City's damaging 1-1 draw against Fulham on Saturday. Maresca's side trailed to Rodrigo Muniz's early opener at the Etihad Stadium before Haaland's equaliser was contentiously ruled out. The City striker kicked the ball out of the grasp of Fulham keeper Bernd Leno on the goal-line. But Leno barely had two hands on the ball when Haaland made contact, giving City reason to feel aggrieved with the decision. Referee Thomas Bramall ruled that Leno had not lost control because the ball was between his hands and VAR Sam Barrott upheld the call. "I reviewed the goal after the game. From my point of view, it's quite clear that it's not a foul, but I'm not the guy that decides, unfortunately," Maresca said. Asked how Haaland viewed the incident, Maresca said: "When they were reviewing the VAR, he was absolutely sure that it was a goal, because I asked him from the touchline. "He was completely sure that it was a goal but the referee decided for different things." Elliot Anderson saved City from a fourth successive league defeat as the England midfielder equalised in the second half with his first top-flight goal since signing from Nottingham Forest in the close-season. But it was another frustrating afternoon for third-placed City, who could not find a winner and were booed off at full-time. Despite the fans' frustration, Maresca tried to accentuate the positives. Anderson's second goal for City in all competitions was a welcome boost after his red card in England's Nations League win against Spain in midweek. "It was a nice moment for him, a nice moment for us because it gave us the chance to come back in the game," Maresca said. "We used him today for the first time as an attacking midfielder. He was playing a little bit more deep with us. "We are trying to find different solutions, the right balance, and to be more consistent." After making a blistering start to the season with seven successive league wins, City are winless in their last four top-flight matches. It was the first time in 15 years and 21 games that City had failed to beat Fulham. Leaders Arsenal can extend their lead over City to eight points if they win at Newcastle later on Saturday. Still waiting to discover the result of their appeal against the guilty verdict over breaches of Premier League financial rules, City have looked increasingly distracted in recent weeks. "For sure we don't like this kind of moments, in terms of four games in a row without a win," Maresca said. "But we also know that, unfortunately, it's normal or it's part of your path that you go through these kind of moments. "It's important that we find a way to keep a clean-sheet. Sometimes you need to win games 1-0." smg/ea
